## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). 3-bets/4-bets extremely wide — including premiums (AA). **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything — including calling multi-street donk-leads with just overcards. C-bets most flops, checks dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); MEDIUM HANDS → checks turn, calls river (station mode); REAL HANDS → shoves aggressively. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **As NON-PFA (BB defend, etc.)**: Fit-or-fold — folds to c-bets when whiffing. Stabs turn with marginal holdings but gives up river on scary boards. **DONK-LEADS with strong made hands (especially in 3-bet pots).** **CHECK-RAISES with semi-bluffs/draws on wet boards** — barrels turn with equity, CHECK-FOLDS river when draw misses. **Key line: P2 check-raise flop → bet turn → check river = BUSTED DRAW — attack with river bet.** Calls 3-bets with pocket pairs (including JJ). **Exploit**: Flat opens IP with suited broadways/connectors. 3-bet QQ+/AKs only. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. DO NOT bluff when P2 is calling with made hands. DO bluff when P2's line = busted draw. As 3-bet caller: c-bet when P2 checks (will fold air); FOLD to P2's donk-lead + turn aggression (strong). **Consistently finishes near bottom ($700-$785 range in recent sessions).**

**Player 3**: **Tight-aggressive, skilled — but consistently loses/finishes bottom half.** Completes SB wide (including QJo), then plays aggressively postflop. 3-bets from blinds vs ALL positions. **Confirmed trapper — wide check-raise range in BOTH 3-bet pots AND limped pots.** Will CHECK-RAISE ALL-IN with as little as top pair in limped pots. C-betting is SELECTIVE. Triple-barrels one-pair value. **Vs RAISED POTS with escalating pressure**: calls flop+turn then folds river to size. **Vs LIMPED/SMALL POTS: stickier AND more aggressive — check-raises with top pair, calls down light.** **Exploit**: Multi-street barrels work in raised pots. In limped pots, don't bluff into P3 — they fight back. Value bet wider in limped pots. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Loose-passive preflop, WILDLY UNPREDICTABLE postflop — part station, part maniac. HIGH VARIANCE player — finishes anywhere from 1st to last.** Calls wide preflop (3-bets with junk, limps wide). **CRITICAL: Capable of MASSIVE bluffs — confirmed shoved all-in with complete air (7-high, no draw) on paired board in limped pot.** Also bets multiway flops with marginal holdings. As LIMPER: Will bet flop AND shove turn with ZERO equity. ALSO still a calling station — calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. **Dual nature: bluffs huge AND calls down light.** PASSIVE with strong made hands — checks made straights through all streets. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+) but folds to 4-bets. 5-BET SHOVE includes JJ.** As single-raiser: C-bets flop, folds to turn raises — FLOATABLE. **Folds SB to button steals with sub-premium hands — confirmed.** **Exploit**: Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target when calling). DON'T auto-fold to P4's aggression in limped pots — can be pure air. CALL DOWN wider vs P4 aggression (especially limped pots). In raised pots as PFA, still floatable. Steal over P4's SB freely. **P4 is the hardest opponent to read — volatile results reflect unpredictable play.**

**Player 5**: **Tight but NOT ultra-nit — VPIP likely ~12-15%.** Confirmed limping KTo in multiway spots. Effective chip accumulator. Even when SHORT-STACKED, 3-bet/shove range remains premium-heavy (confirmed AA at ~5.5BB). **Will STAB multiway flops with just overcards/backdoor draws (semi-bluff style).** C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. **As CALLER facing aggression: will call ONE street then FOLDS to continued betting, especially with scare cards.** Donk-bets can be strong OR weak — weak ones fold to raises/turn barrels; strong ones ESCALATE. **ANY turn raise from P5 = monster.** **PASSIVE WITH STRONG MADE HANDS — just flat-calls with straights on river.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Multi-street value bet gets only 1-2 streets max — size up earlier streets. FOLD to P5's turn raises always. Good steal target in blinds. **P5's 3-bets are ALWAYS strong regardless of stack depth.**

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wide limper, opener, AND cold-caller.** **As LIMPER: EXTREMELY sticky postflop — calls with bottom pair, A-high through multiple streets. Folds preflop to large raises/steals.** **Flop donk-leads = likely air/weak draws → RAISE for fold equity. RIVER donk-leads after check-calling = VALUE → respect.** **CHECK-CALLS with real made hands throughout — passive line = actual hand.** **RAISES/RE-RAISES can be SEMI-BLUFFS with combo draws.** MASSIVE overbets = value. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED.** **Confirmed folds BB AND SB to button steals.** **Exploit**: Value bet wide — P6 calls down with any piece including A-high. SIZE DOWN iso-raises (~3x) to keep P6 in when you have value. NEVER bluff check-calling P6. RAISE flop donk-leads. RESPECT river donk-leads. FOLD to 4-bet shoves/overbets. Steal over P6's blinds freely. **P6 consistently finishes near bottom — typically last or second-to-last.**

**Player 7**: **CONFIRMED extremely wide opener — opens trash hands (T3o from MP).** Wide limper too. **PREFLOP MANIAC in escalated pots** — limp-3bets with suited broadways (KQs confirmed), calls 5-bets with QQ/suited junk, 6-bets with weak aces. **Limp-raise range is VERY wide: any Ax, pocket pairs, AND suited broadways.** **Postflop**: Commits with made hands (two pair+) — will 3-bet flop and call off. **Exploit**: Iso-raise wide over P7's opens/limps — HIGHLY +EV. Value bet relentlessly. In reraised pots, get it in with any premium. **P7 consistently BUSTS or finishes last across nearly every session — ultimate dead money source.**

## Opponent Profiles

### Player 1 – Disciplined TAG (Value-Leaning, Structured Aggression)
- Solid open ranges; capable of open/folding to 3-bets.
- 4-bet range remains tight and premium-heavy.
- Linear 3-bet structure with broadways and medium+ pairs.
- Donk leads skew top-pair+.
- Double barrels turns for value on dynamic boards.
- River aggression is strongly value-weighted.
- Comfortable applying pressure when checked to in bloated pots; preflop flats do not imply passivity.
- In multiway pots, continued aggression still deserves substantial respect; pressure is not auto-capped just because ranges are wider.

**Exploit:**
- Increase IP 3-bets.
- Apply pressure when his range is capped.
- Avoid light 5-bets and thin river hero calls.
- Give more respect to large bets in bloated/multiway pots.

---

### Player 3 – Loose Recreational (Wide Stack-Off / Nonstandard Preflop Aggression)
- Calls preflop all-ins far too wide, including dominated and weak holdings.
- Loose hand selection; fold equity versus him is poor.
- Bluff-catches at reasonable sizing.
- Postflop tends passive unless connected, but preflop can take splashy, nonstandard aggressive lines.
- Weird small raises are not premium-only.
- Can cold re-raise light in multiway spots, including weak ace-x/blocker-type hands.

**Exploit:**
- Value jam wider, especially over odd/small preflop re-raises.
- Greatly reduce bluff jams.
- Do not rely on fold equity once he has shown interest.
- Treat unusual preflop aggression as wide and under-structured, not strong by default.
- Value bet thinner postflop.

---

### Player 4 – Structured TAG (Strong Value Raises)
- Tight preflop discipline.
- Flop raises in single-raised pots are heavily value-weighted.
- 3-bets/4-bets skew premium.
- Will call short-stack shoves wider than expected when covering.

**Exploit:**
- Overfold to flop raises without strong equity.
- Avoid light postflop 3-bet bluffs.
- Value shove appropriately when shallow.

---

### Player 5 – Passive TAG / Protection-Oriented, Slowplay Capable
- Limp/calls include pocket pairs and some offsuit broadway/high-card hands.
- Donk-leads with medium-strength hands and draws using merged sizing, including multiway.
- Flop checks do not cap range; can slowplay strong hands.
- Small/medium turn leads are merged, not purely weak.
- Turn barrels after earlier aggression can still contain draws.
- River aggression is extremely value-heavy.
- After earlier aggression, river checks often indicate medium strength and some foldability.

**Exploit:**
- Don’t auto-attack flop checks.
- Be selective floating turn leads.
- Overfold to river bets.
- Apply pressure more often when he checks river after leading earlier streets.

---

### Player 6 – Loose-Passive with Merged River Stabs
- Limp/calls wide.
- Calls preflop all-ins lighter than population when covering.
- Generally passive postflop.
- Passive flop/turn continue ranges can include weak made hands, ace-high floats, and strong draws.
- River leads after passive lines are merged: bluff, thin value, or blocker/value bets appear.
- Still willing to call down with medium strength.

**Exploit:**
- Do not auto-overfold to river leads, especially on scare cards.
- Treat river leads as merged rather than strictly polarized.
- Bluff-catch based on blockers/runout.
- Avoid thin raises versus river leads unless holding clear value.
- Stay value-heavy versus his calling tendencies.

---

### Player 7 – Loose-Passive, Sticky Bluff-Catcher
- Limp-heavy preflop.
- Small turn donk bets can be blocking bets with medium pairs, not just weak draws.
- Will bluff-catch river with medium-strength hands.
- River betting is still more value-heavy than bluff-heavy, but calling ranges are wider than initially assumed.
- Can continue one street and release on later scary runouts or stronger second barrels; stickiness is not unlimited.

**Exploit:**
- Continue isolating preflop.
- Reduce assumptions that small donks = weakness.
- Bluff rivers less when he has shown earlier-street interest.
- Value bet confidently when ahead.
- Apply turn pressure selectively on bad runouts for bluff-catchers.
